searchText: b"h phase three — final execution specification boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos is not revealed by clutter but by order that lets intention flow; awtsmoos.com should hide needless machinery while making every needed pathway glow. final architecture contract a. surface isolation every migrated page has one explicit root attribute/class. every authored selector lives beneath that root. entry css files contain only @import statements plus, if unavoidable, a documented root declaration. shared css modules never style arbitrary document elements globally. b. css module families keep modules focused and small: tokens: local colors, typography, spacing, radius, shadows, z layers foundation: box sizing and typography scoped to the surface root layout: shell, containers, grids, stacks, overflow behavior controls: buttons, links, fields, toggles, summaries panels: cards, drawers, dialogs, notices, toolbars states: hover, active, focus visible, disabled, busy, selected, expanded motion: transitions/keyframes plus reduced motion contract responsive: mobile first enhancements at explicit breakpoints c. javascript architecture use technically precise torah/kabbalah names only where the mapping clarifies responsibility. a genuine lifecycle hierarchy may progress from static vessel to reactive controller; services such as api transport, validation, serialization, and rendering remain separate composed collaborators. every nontrivial declaration receives full jsdoc. suggested responsibility mapping when truthful: gevurah... — validation/permission/bounds tiferes... — orchestration/reconciliation netzach... — persistence/retry/durable state hod... — formatting/reporting/serialization yesod... — transport/repository/integration malchus... — rendering/user visible manifestation d. interaction contract every relevant interactive control must define: default state hover state on hover capable devices focus visible state active/pressed state disabled state where applicable selected/expanded state where applicable loading/busy state where applicable no interaction may depend on hover alone. e. mobile and overlay contract mobile is the base layout. no component may require horizontal page scrolling. drawers/panels must retract cleanly and restore focus. overlays own one bounded stacking context. z index values come from local tokens, not arbitrary escalation. fixed elements respect safe area insets where relevant. content children use wrapping/min width protections. f. api contract for touched browser/api paths, explicitly separate validation, transport, normalization, error translation, and rendering. preserve existing public request/response contracts unless all consumers are intentionally migrated and verified. g. documentation contract docs must describe real current behavior: page family architecture, css scoping rules, interaction/state requirements, javascript module boundaries, api/error conventions, and verification commands. aspirational behavior remains labeled as planned. first implementation wave 1. establish git/uncommitted change evidence. 2. discover local instructions and common dependencies. 3. inspect static, auth, docs/catalog, social/app, and api representatives. 4. extract only recurring primitives proven by those pages. 5. build scoped css foundation and shared js contracts. 6. rewrite complete representative files and their imports. 7. verify before expanding to compatible siblings. 8. expand family by family while updating 00 remaining work.md. 9. finish docs from verified implementation. 10. perform whole pass browser/static/build review. definition of better the result is better only when it is visibly clearer, measurably safer against style collisions and overflow, easier to navigate with touch and keyboard, easier to extend through explicit modules/contracts, and backed by real verification rather than aesthetic claims.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem — blessed is he awtsmoos renews every instant, and this interface should feel renewed without noise; awtsmoos.com should reveal depth on demand, while calmness is what first shows. phase one — chessed vision mission: transform the geelooy social experience into a mobile first, fast, restrained, futuristic system whose advanced capabilities unfold only when requested. primary surfaces: social feed, social hub, composer, actions, profile, aliases, heichel/heichelos, series/post reader, comments, notifications, editors, navigation, and shared social data/api helpers. experience laws: mobile first; nothing may overflow the viewport every interactive control must have deliberate hover, focus visible, active, disabled, loading, and error states advanced controls collapse into contextual drawers, menus, accordions, or sheets animation should clarify state, never delay interaction no global selector leakage; each page/component owns a namespaced style boundary z index values come from a small documented layer scale typography, spacing, radius, elevation, and motion derive from local tokens dense pages gain progressive disclosure instead of permanent chrome apis return predictable data and ui state maps cleanly to loading/success/empty/error states potential high value improvements: feed density modes, sticky contextual actions, resilient skeletons, optimistic interactions, keyboard focus systems, reader progress, alias identity switcher, heichel discovery cards, series continuity, reduced motion support, safe area support, container aware layouts, and mobile bottom sheet actions.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem — blessed is he from boundless light the vessels receive a measured line; a clean interface becomes stronger when every boundary is fine. phase two — architecture candidates a. page local css only: safest isolation, but repeated patterns can drift. b. shared global design system: fastest consistency, but violates the no global conflict requirement unless every selector is namespaced. c. namespaced feature capsules: each surface imports local tokens, primitives, motion, and page rules beneath a unique root class. this is the preferred foundation. d. shadow dom custom elements: strongest isolation, but migration cost and existing dom/api coupling may be too high. e. inline component styles: isolation is acceptable but maintainability and caching are weaker for this codebase. preferred direction: c, with optional d only for self contained future widgets. javascript direction: small classes with explicit contracts; data driven state descriptors; shared transport/adapters separated from renderers; event coordination separated from dom querying; inheritance only for genuine lifecycle families. verification target: route by route browser evidence at narrow mobile, wide mobile, tablet, and desktop widths; console errors; overflow detection; focus traversal; api failures; reduced motion; touch target sizing; and regression checks for existing user flows.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem — blessed is he chessed expands and gevurah defines, tiferes makes the pattern align; the awtsmoos gives each vessel purpose, so beauty and function can shine. phase three — critique and improvements thirty concrete safeguards/improvements: 1. inventory all social entry routes before styling 2. trace css imports before adding new imports 3. detect broad element selectors that can leak 4. detect duplicate class names across features 5. establish namespaced roots per surface 6. establish local token files 7. document a restrained z layer scale 8. audit fixed/sticky positioning 9. audit horizontal overflow at 320px 10. honor safe area insets 11. preserve semantic html 12. add focus visible treatment 13. preserve keyboard activation 14. use minimum practical touch targets 15. add disabled/loading states 16. add empty/error states 17. add reduced motion fallbacks 18. avoid animation on layout critical properties where possible 19. remove duplicated listeners 20. centralize fetch/error normalization 21. avoid hidden implicit globals 22. make api response parsing defensive 23. keep dom renderers separate from transport 24. keep touched executable modules compact 25. preserve public exports and routes 26. test alias identity switching 27. test series reader continuation 28. test heichel navigation depth 29. test feed interactions under slow/failing api responses 30. re read every touched file and compare planned versus actual behavior decision: begin with shared social infrastructure and the most used public surfaces, then fan outward to editors and secondary pages after browser evidence confirms the foundation.
